blindSummary: The wealthiest, most urbanised state/province wrapping the federal capital is not a safe harbour. In January 2026 the state government declared it would not allow LGBT promotion and called for an investigation into a pride-themed gathering; in December 2025 the state's hereditary ruler used Friday sermons at mosques to warn against LGBT practices — the monarchy-plus-religious-bureaucracy channel operating statewide. The state's religious department is the agency that pursued a well-known transgender entrepreneur with an arrest warrant and an all-out manhunt over her presentation, mobilising 122 religious affairs officers, an episode that drew national attention to cross-dressing enforcement here. Countervailing: it also has a documented record of prosecutions for violence against trans people — after a 32-year-old trans woman was beaten to death in a city in 2018, four suspects were arrested and charged.
